prompt:
Add a `tasklist` extension: a list item whose text starts with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` followed by a space becomes a task.
- The marker is replaced by `<input type="checkbox">`, `checked` for `x`/`X`, and `disabled` unless the `clickable` option is true (default false).
- The `<li>` gets the class from the `item_class` option (default `task`).
- It works in ordered and unordered lists, nested lists and loose lists, and keeps inline markup after the marker.
Register it so `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` works once installed.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
I added the `tasklist` extension and `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` loads it. The full test suite passes: 1144 tests run, 112 skipped, none failing. List items starting with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` and a space get a checkbox, which is `checked` for x/X and `disabled` unless `clickable=True`. The `
  • ` gets the `item_class` class (default `task`). It works in ordered, unordered, nested and loose lists (in a loose list the checkbox goes inside the first `

    `), and inline markup after the marker still renders. The extension is registered in `pyproject.toml` and the fixture's `entry_points.txt`. I also added tests, a docs page, a reference page, navigation and index entries, and an unreleased changelog entry (it has no issue number because there isn't an issue). flake8 isn't installed here, so I checked line lengths by hand instead of running it.
